$comment: Structural-rejection fixture — see schemas/conformance/README.md 'Structural-rejection fixtures'. The chain-step, chain-hash, and outer-signature placeholders (__ANY_*__, __VALID_GRANT_PROOF_SIG__) are intentional and never resolved: a v0.1 implementation MUST reject the non-empty `chain` field at the early structural check, before any per-hop signature work. This fixture is NOT dynamic. FROZEN in the v0.1 wire shape: this fixture's input deliberately keeps the v0.1 embedded-signature token (delegator/grant_proof/chain-of-objects) and the retired v0.1 placeholders so v0.1 runners keep a pinned vector. It is NOT migrated to aitp/0.3; the v0.2 structural-rejection equivalent (compact-JWS token with a `chain` claim) is del-007-multihop-rejected-v02.
description: A delegation token whose `chain` field is non-empty MUST be rejected by a v0.1 implementation with DELEGATION_MULTIHOP_NOT_SUPPORTED, regardless of any other validity property of the token. RFC-AITP-0006 v0.1 forbade multi-hop verification; the chain field is the trigger. The runner MUST reject before performing any per-hop signature work — the multi-hop rejection is a structural/early check, not the result of failed verification. Multi-hop acceptance semantics are reserved for RFC-AITP-0011 (Draft, opt-in) and exercised by the `del-mh-*` fixture set. This fixture is frozen in the v0.1 wire shape and is required only for v0.1 runners; v0.2 runners use del-007-multihop-rejected-v02, the claim-shaped sibling that pins the same DELEGATION_MULTIHOP_NOT_SUPPORTED behavior for the aitp/0.3 compact-JWS token.

expected.rationale: The `chain` field is non-empty. A v0.1 implementation MUST reject before any signature, scope, or chain-hash verification is performed. The placeholder values for chain-step / chain-hash / outer signatures are deliberate: this fixture asserts the early structural check, not failed cryptographic verification.
